title: Introduce CI attenuator and dependency sieve to reduce presubmit noise
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Our presubmit lanes have grown noisy and expensive: a small class of changes (docs, markdown tweaks, single-package comments) still trigger the heaviest integration lanes which increases queue time and CI cost. Separate but related, repo dependency churn produces a lot of incidental dependency PRs and transient failures during lockfile refresh. Motivation: add a lightweight, deterministic filter (CI attenuator) that narrows which CI lanes run based on a change impact profile and introduce a dependency-sieve utility that produces curated, minimal dependency refresh PRs to reduce churn and make upgrade PRs easier to review. Goals: 1) Reduce expensive presubmit runs for low-impact changes while preserving strong coverage for risky edits. 2) Make dependency updates quieter and auditable by vendorizing minimal manifests and surfacing only risky transitive changes. 3) Keep the implementation small and reversible. Summary of changes (single pass): - Add tools/ci/attenuator.go: a small Go service used by the presubmit router to compute a lane-set based on a change manifest and a configurable rule table. Rules include path globs, owner hints, and a risk score threshold. - Update .github/workflows/ci.yaml: wire a new lightweight 'presubmit-eval' job that calls the attenuator and emits a JSON artifact with lanes to run. - Add scripts/dep_sieve.py: a small Python utility to produce curated dependency update PRs. It computes the minimal upgrade set, vendorizes the changed modules into deps/vendor/* and generates a tidy changelog fragment. - Introduce tools/ci/rules.yaml: default attenuation rules used in the first rollout. - Add tests and CI harness: tests/attenuator_test.go and tests/dep_sieve_test.py with deterministic fixtures. - Add docs: docs/ci/attenuator.md and docs/ci/dep_sieve.md with rollout and rollback instructions. Checklist: - [x] Attenuator core logic implemented and unit-tested - [x] CI job integration and artifact handoff - [x] Dep-sieve minimal upgrade generation implemented and tested - [x] Small canary rollout config (run on infra and sdk directories first) - [x] Observability hooks (metrics and debug logging) - [x] Documentation and rollback steps Review notes: This PR is intentionally additive; the attenuator only gates which existing jobs run and never disables job execution paths, so it is reversible by updating rules.yaml. The dep_sieve generates PR branches; maintainers can examine vendorized diffs before merge. Backwards compatibility: No API changes in runtime or SDKs. Rollout plan: initial canary on infra/, sdk-go/ with attenuation conservative thresholds (risk_score > 0.8 required for heavy integration lanes) for two weeks, then relax thresholds if stable. Related: ENG-3012 (CI cost reduction), ENG-3089 (dep hygiene).

Maya Chen (2025-11-06): Addressed both: added precedence doc and tests; added metrics via prometheus client and a small /debug endpoint for local inspection.

Sandeep Rao (2025-11-07): Dep-sieve looks promising. Please ensure vendorization step is gated behind a --dry-run by default in CI to avoid accidental large diffs; also prefer an incremental vendor path instead of full rewrite.
Maya Chen (2025-11-08): Implemented --dry-run default and incremental vendor logic. Added an approval gate comment in generated PRs with a human reviewer checklist.

Evan Brooks (2025-11-10): Observability: add a histogram for latency of the attenuator decision (we saw up to 250ms in local bench). Also suggest conservative default risk thresholds in rules.yaml. Approved after changes.

merge_commit_message:
Squash: introduce ci attenuator + dep_sieve to reduce presubmit cost and dependency churn

- add attenuator decision engine and test harness
- wire presubmit-eval job and artifact passing
- add dep_sieve generator (dry-run by default)
- docs and rollout notes

Rollout: canary on infra/ and sdk-go/ for 2 weeks
release_notes:
- Add CI attenuator to reduce heavy presubmit runs for low-impact changes (can be tuned via tools/ci/rules.yaml).
- Introduce dep_sieve: generates curated, vendorized minimal dependency update PRs (dry-run by default in CI).
- Observability: metrics for attenuation decisions and latency added.
notes_for_maintainers: Rollout: start canary on infra/ and sdk-go/ with current rules.yaml. To revert immediately, set tools/ci/rules.yaml default_allow_all: true or remove presubmit-eval step from CI. Dep_sieve will only create draft PRs in dry-run mode; to enable actual branch creation set --apply in maintenance windows. Monitor metric: ci_attenuator_skipped_total and ci_attenuator_decision_latency_seconds.
changelog_fragment: CI: add attenuator and dep_sieve for presubmit throttling and curated dep updates (ENG-3012, ENG-3089).
file_snippets:
.github/workflows/ci.yaml snippet: 
  presubmit-eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run attenuator
        run: go run tools/ci/attenuator.go --changes $CHANGES --out lanes.json
      - name: Upload lanes
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: lanes.json
          path: lanes.json

scripts/dep_sieve.py snippet: 
# dry-run mode by default
if __name__ == '__main__':
  parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
  parser.add_argument('--apply', action='store_true')
  # compute minimal upgrade set and write vendor/
audit_notes: Added small surface area in tools/ci and a new workflow job. No runtime code changes. Added vendor artifacts under deps/vendor for dep PRs; these are generated only in dep_sieve --apply mode. All new binaries are built with existing CI toolchain.
post_merge_tasks:
- Monitor ci_attenuator_skipped_total and decision latency for 7 days
- Gradually expand canary to other high-traffic directories
- Run dep_sieve in scheduled weekly mode for low-risk ecosystem updates
safety_and_rollback: This change is additive and configurable. To rollback: (1) revert .github/workflows/ci.yaml presubmit-eval job, or (2) set tools/ci/rules.yaml to conservative defaults (allow_all: true). Dep_sieve is non-destructive by default (dry-run); no rollback required unless --apply was used in error.
